tools/bolt: "has a smooth unthreaded shank below the head on longer sizes": true of partially threaded hex bolts, but fully threaded long bolts (tap bolts) also exist
"is often made of hardened metal with a zinc coating": common for general-purpose grade bolts; many are plain, black-oxide or stainless instead
tools/hoe: "is still the main hand implement on many African smallholdings": widely reported for sub-Saharan smallholder farming; a general claim, not checked against a specific source
tools/knife: "is laid to the right of a dinner plate at the table": Western table-setting convention, not universal
tools/needle: "can be magnetized and floated on a leaf as a compass": the standard survival improvisation; it works for small needles, alignment is weak
tools/rake: "is used by croupiers to gather chips across a gaming table": true for roulette and baccarat; craps uses a hooked stick that may not count as the same object
"comes in a wide aluminium version for spreading hot asphalt": the asphalt rake/lute is a paving-trade item that a lay reader may not know
tools/saw: "cuts on the pull stroke rather than the push in some Asian designs": certain for traditional Japanese designs; less certain how widely it holds elsewhere in Asia
tools/sponge: "stiffens when dry and softens again once wet": true of cellulose sponges; polyurethane foam sponges stay fairly soft when dry
"is thrown away and replaced every few weeks for hygiene": common hygiene advice (weekly to monthly), not what every household does
tools/vise: "grips round pipe in curved notches below its main jaws": true of combination/pipe-jaw bench vises, not every model
"often has a small flat anvil area behind its rear jaw": common on engineer's bench vises, absent on woodworking vises
